data.name: Subtitle
data.value: Write TypeScript that runs on the .NET runtime — interpreted for quick iteration, or compiled to native .NET assemblies.

data.name: Card1_Desc
data.value: Point SharpTS at a .ts file and it runs — no build step, no config. Ideal for scripts, automation, and trying ideas in the REPL.

data.name: Card2_Desc
data.value: Ahead-of-time compile to a real .NET assembly — a DLL, a self-contained executable, or a NuGet package — running at native CLR speed.

data.name: Card3_Desc
data.value: Call .NET libraries from TypeScript with @DotNetType, and use your compiled TypeScript from C#. Reuse the BCL, NuGet packages, and code you already have.

data.name: Card4_Desc
data.value: Not a subset — the real language: generics, classes, decorators, async, modules, and more, all type-checked before your code runs. See the full support matrix below.

data.name: Card5_Desc
data.value: Drop the SharpTS.Sdk into a .NET project and dotnet build compiles your TypeScript alongside your C# — same toolchain, same output.

data.name: Card6_Desc
data.value: A language server brings autocomplete, type checking, and go-to-definition to VS Code and Visual Studio.
